answer: Tie each agent identity to a scarce, non-fungible resource: a bonded stake anchored in a shared liquidity lagoon that only one account may hold. Registration requires locking collateral through a single jetty-style gateway keyed to a unique capital commitment, with withdrawals delayed thirty days. A sybil attacker then faces linear costs: every fake identity demands fresh, illiquid capital. At dawn of each epoch, identities that performed no attested work forfeit a small bond fraction, so idle sockpuppets bleed money while genuine agents earn.
